clinician.trajectory_summary: An immunocompromised patient (post-kidney transplant on prednisone and sodium mycophenolate) presented with a one-year history of subcutaneous nodules, fever, cough, and weight loss. A biopsy of a subcutaneous nodule on the right arm revealed cellular tissue with proliferation of macrophages and rare multinucleated giant cells, in addition to lymphoplasma neutrophilic infiltrate. Methenamine silver staining showed a great quantity of intracytoplasmatic microorganisms characteristic of H. capsulatum, sometimes forming hyphae and spores, confirming the diagnosis of histoplasmosis. The systemic symptoms in an immunocompromised host, along with the biopsy findings, support the diagnosis of disseminated histoplasmosis.
